On 7–9 September, India's SEBI Demat 2.0 pilot recorded three native DLT corporate bond issuances totaling ₹1,025 crore on NSDL and CDSL platforms. REC placed ₹500 crore with 18 investors, L&T Finance ₹500 crore with four, and IIFL Finance ₹25 crore with one. Atomic DvP settlement occurred through the RBI wholesale CBDC (e₹-W) on the Unified Market Interface, while each instrument retained full conventional legal rights. Because issuance and settlement operate inside regulated depository rails rather than crypto venues, the pilot creates a direct on-chain channel for corporate debt without requiring new legal constructs. This extends tokenized instruments beyond T-bill experiments into India's $620–700 billion corporate bond market, beginning with institutional participants. Later phases will add RFQ secondary trading and retail access. Volume and settlement data from these issuances will indicate scalability of the combined DLT-CBDC model.

今日かなり気になった
インド×RWA×中央銀行マネーのニュースです👀

インドというだけで
少し遠い市場に見えるかもしれませんが・・・
今回の話は
 「証券をトークン化しました」だけではありません

インド証券取引委員会
SEBI が
約6200億ドル規模の社債市場を背景に
Demat 2.0
という実証を始めました

まず数字だけ見ると・・・
「6200億ドルの社債が全部オンチェーン化？」
と思ってしまいますが
そこは違います

市場全体
↓
約6200億ドル規模

今回の初期実証
↓
 1025クロールピー
＝102.5億ルピー

です

参加したのは・・・
・REC
・Larsen & Toubro
・IIFL Finance
の3社
なので現段階では
まだパイロットです

それでも今回
私が一押ししたい理由は・・・
証券だけではなく
「支払うお金」まで同じデジタル基盤へ載せたこと
です
ここがかなり大きいです

RWAやトークン化証券では・・・

社債
↓
トークン化

株式
↓
トークン化

ファンド
↓
トークン化

という話をよく見ます
でも・・・
証券だけ速く動いても

代金の支払いが・・・

銀行送金
↓
営業時間待ち

照合
↓
確認

決済
↓
後から

では
取引全体は
まだ完全にはデジタル化されません

そこでインドが今回使うのが・・・
デジタルルピー
です

しかもこれは
USDT
USDC
のような民間ステーブルコインではなく
インド準備銀行
RBIが発行する中央銀行デジタル通貨
です

流れを見ると・・・

トークン化社債
↓
投資家へ移転

同時に・・・

デジタルルピー
↓
売り手へ移転

そして
両方成功した時だけ取引成立
という仕組みを使います

これが
アトミックDvP
です

DvPは
Delivery versus Payment
日本語では
証券の受け渡しと
代金の支払いを連動させる仕組み
です

簡単にすると・・・

証券だけ渡った
↓
でもお金が来ない

お金だけ払った
↓
でも証券が来ない

これを防ぐために・・・

証券
＋
お金
↓
同時に交換
します

今回さらに面白いのは
その「お金」の側が
中央銀行マネーだということです

つまり・・・

トークン化証券
×
中央銀行デジタル通貨
を
同じ決済工程へ載せています

ここまで来ると
「ブロックチェーンで社債を発行しました」
より・・・
資本市場の決済インフラそのものを
作り替えようとしている
と見る方が近い気がします

そしてインドの設計は
既存金融を全部捨てて
新しい暗号資産市場を作る
という形でもありません

むしろ・・・

既存の証券口座
↓
残す

KYC
↓
残す

証券預託機関
↓
残す

既存の取引基盤
↓
残す

その裏側で・・・

所有記録
決済
利払い
償還
↓
分散型台帳へ接続

していきます
ここも重要です

最近のRWAニュースを追っていると
「ブロックチェーンが既存金融を置き換える」
というより・・・
既存金融のバックエンドへ
ブロックチェーンが入り込む
動きが増えています

今回のインドは
そのかなり分かりやすい事例です

もう一つ気になったのが
法的な所有権を誰が持つのか
です

今回トークン化されても・・・
社債の

・ISIN
・利率
・満期
・格付け
・契約条件
・投資家権利
は
そのまま維持されます
そして正式な所有記録も
引き続き
インドの証券預託機関が担います

つまり・・・
「暗号資産っぽい新商品」を作った
のではなく
既存の社債そのものを
新しい記録・決済方式へ移す
という設計です
ここは
前に見たSECの移転代理人の話とも少し似ています

トークンを作れる
↓
だけでは足りない

誰が正式な保有者？
↓
必要

誰が記録する？
↓
必要

代金はどう払う？
↓
必要

決済はいつ確定？
↓
必要

です

さらに・・・
投資家自身が
秘密鍵を管理する必要もありません

預託機関
↓
鍵を管理

投資家
↓
既存に近い証券口座で利用

という形です
なので・・・
ブロックチェーンを使う
＝
全員がウォレットと秘密鍵を自分で管理
でもありません

ここは機関投資家には
かなり大きいと思います
そして今回
個人的に一番気になったのは・・・
証券とお金が
初めて“同じ時間軸”へ近づいたこと
です

これまで・・・

トークン化債券
↓
24時間動ける

でも・・・

決済用の銀行マネー
↓
営業時間や既存決済網に依存

となると
最後のお金のところで
止まる可能性があります
ところが・・・

社債
↓
デジタル化

銀行マネー
↓
デジタルルピー

両方
↓
同時決済

となれば
資産とお金を
同じデジタル時間軸
へ載せられる可能性があります

これはRWA市場では
かなり大きなテーマです

たとえば今後・・・

トークン化国債
↓
24時間

トークン化社債
↓
24時間

トークン化ファンド
↓
24時間

でも

支払いのお金
↓
止まる
なら

市場全体は
24時間にはなりません

だから・・・
資産のトークン化
だけでなく
決済資産のデジタル化
も必要になります

インドは今回
そこをセットで試し始めました

今後は・・・

第2段階
↓
流通市場

個人投資家
↓
拡張

第3段階
↓
参加ノード・対象商品の拡大

が検討されています

なので見るべきなのは・・・
「6200億ドル市場！」
という大きな数字だけではなく
102.5億ルピーの実証が
本当に二次流通へつながるか
です

そして・・・

大量取引
↓
耐えられる？

障害
↓
どう復旧？

サイバー攻撃
↓
どう対応？

利払い
↓
自動化できる？

償還
↓
安定して処理できる？

個人投資家
↓
使える？

ここが次の確認ポイントです
インドのニュースは
日本では少し注目されにくいですが・・・

今回については
「社債をトークン化した」
ではなく
「証券と中央銀行マネーを
同時に動かす資本市場を試し始めた」
と見ると
かなり見え方が変わると思います

RWAの次の競争は
何をトークン化した？
から・・・
「資産とお金を

へ進んでいるのかもしれません

John 14:8–9 does not say Jesus is God.

Philip asks Jesus, “Lord, show us the Father,” and Jesus replies, “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.” In context, Jesus is explaining that he perfectly represents and reveals the Father—not saying that he is literally the same person as the Father.

In fact, the same Gospel repeatedly distinguishes Jesus from God:

Jesus says, “The Father is greater than I.” (John 14:28)

He also says, “This is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” (John 17:3)

And after his resurrection: “I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.” (John 20:17)

As for Revelation 1:8, the speaker is identified as “the Lord God… the Almighty”, not explicitly as Jesus. The surrounding passage distinguishes “God” from “Jesus Christ” (Revelation 1:1–2).

Revelation 1:17–18 says, “I am the First and the Last… I was dead, and behold I am alive forevermore.” This is indeed spoken by the risen Jesus in the passage. But saying Jesus has a divine title or attribute is not the same as Jesus explicitly saying, “I am God.” That is the theological conclusion that Christians draw from the text.

So again, let’s distinguish between what Jesus explicitly says and what later theology concludes from certain titles and passages.

Jesus explicitly calls the Father “the only true God” (John 17:3) and calls the Father “my God” (John 20:17). Those statements deserve to be considered alongside the passages being presented as proof of Jesus’ divinity.

By 2030, one of the most fundamental assumptions of modern society may begin to disappear: the idea that people must belong to a company in order to work.
AI agents, robotics, automation, cloud computing, and blockchain are transforming far more than productivity. A new model is beginning to emerge.

The company is not an eternal institution.

What happens when the organization itself begins to disappear?

2030 may not be the year every company vanishes. But it could become the moment when humanity realizes that society may no longer require the traditional company to function.

Demat 2.0 is not just Demat upgraded. It is finance becoming programmable.

SEBI and RBI’s Demat 2.0 pilot tokenises corporate bonds on a permissioned DLT network, while the e-Rupee handles the cash leg.

The important part is not simply speed.

Bond + money can move simultaneously, reducing settlement risk, reconciliation and layers of back-office intermediaries.

More importantly, the bond itself becomes programmable. Smart contracts can eventually automate interest payments, redemptions and other servicing, turning a traditionally paperwork-heavy process into software.

And tokenisation changes the economics of access. As the system scales, bonds can potentially be fractionalised into smaller units, making an asset class historically dominated by institutions accessible to retail investors.

The pilot has already processed over ₹1,025 crore, involving issuers such as REC, L&T and IIFL Finance.

But this is bigger than corporate bonds.

India is effectively testing the rails for an onchain financial market, with the same infrastructure potentially extending to equities, funds, gold and other real-world assets.

1/ On 11 Sept 2026, Metropolitan Stock Exchange put
out a press release.

Remember that name. 🧵

2/ The release reads like a milestone.

SEBI Chairman and RBI Governor launching the pilot
at Global Fintech Fest. Distributed ledger. CBDC
settlement. India's first tokenised bonds.

If you hold MSE shares, this looked like the news
you'd waited a decade for.

3/ So let's start with what an EBP actually is.

Any private placement of debt securities of ₹20 cr
or more MUST route through a registered Electronic
Book Provider. It's mandatory.

There are four: NSE, BSE, MSE, NSDL.

MSE has held this licence since 2016.

4/ Ten years with the licence.

FY26 operating revenue: ₹3.4 crore

FY26 net loss: ₹25.8 crore

NSE did ₹25,785 cr within two months of launching
in 2016. Today it holds ~95% of the debt RFQ market.

So what went wrong?

5/ Not the licence. MSE always had permission.

Bond issuance runs on relationships. An arranger who
trusts you. An ops team that answers at 9 PM when a
bid file breaks.

That takes people. People take money.

Nobody funds a bond desk on ₹3.4 cr of revenue.

6/ And Demat 2.0 doesn't fix that.

The ledger belongs to the depositories.

The cash rail belongs to RBI.

The exchange runs the bidding screen.

MSE got a better back office. So did NSE and BSE.

The same day.

Tokenisation is not a moat.

7/ So we stopped reading press releases and opened
MSE's private placement filings.

Jan 2025: ₹238 cr. Groww's parent, Rainmatter
(Zerodha), Securocrop, Share India.

29,75,00,000 shares each. Exactly equal.

Aug 2025: ₹1,000 cr offered to 29 offerees.

8/ ₹1,238 crore total. Roughly 365x annual
operating revenue.

And read those 29 names — it stops looking like a
venture round.

Monarch Networth. Marwadi Chandarana. KIFS. Findoc.
Excel. Achintya. StockGro. Mansi Share.

A broker consortium with a venture fund attached.

9/ Then we got to number fourteen on the list.

Trust Investment Advisors Private Limited, BKC.  The same arranger from the press release in tweet 1.  

Equity offered August 2025. Deal delivered September 2026.  

10/ That one line item is the whole story.  

MSE didn't win that deal on technology ,NSE and BSE got the identical rail on the identical day.  

It won because someone in the bond market finally had a reason to pick up the phone.  That's what ₹1,238 crore actually bought.  

11/ The honest caveat:  

The mechanism has worked exactly once. One arranger. One deal. ₹25 crore. One investor.  MSE's slice of the ₹1,025 cr pilot was 2.4%.  

A real signal. 

Not a turnaround.

#NSDL LAUNCHES DEMAT 2.0 FOR TOKENISED SECURITIES AND CBDC SETTLEMENT

National Securities Depository Limited has launched Demat 2.0, a next-generation platform that supports tokenised securities and enables near-instant settlement through the Reserve Bank of India's wholesale Central Bank Digital Currency.
The initiative forms part of a joint SEBI-RBI pilot for tokenised corporate bonds, unveiled at the Global Fintech Fest 2026 by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra and SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey.
In an interview at the event, an NSDL official described Demat 2.0 as the next step after the original dematerialisation system introduced about 30 years ago. Demat 1.0 replaced physical share certificates with electronic records. This improved settlement speed, reduced disputes and built greater trust in the market. Settlement cycles gradually shortened from several days or weeks to the current T+1 cycle, with optional T+0 available in some segments.
Demat 2.0 extends that framework. It operates on a blockchain platform and uses two linked wallets: a securities wallet that holds the tokens and a currency wallet that holds the wholesale CBDC (digital rupee).
Under the process, an issuer creates bond tokens. Investors subscribe and successful bidders receive allocation. The tokens are credited to the investor's Demat 2.0 account. Simultaneously, the corresponding CBDC amount is transferred in an atomic delivery-versus-payment mechanism. The investor parts with money and receives the securities at the same moment. There is no time lag between the two legs of the transaction.
This instantaneous settlement reduces settlement risk compared with the existing system, where a gap remains between payment and delivery. The official compared the difference to that between NEFT and IMPS, or to the speed of UPI.
The platform is currently in pilot mode and limited to bond tokens. Later stages are expected to add trading capabilities and expand to other instruments, subject to regulatory approvals and market maturity. Investors continue to use their existing demat accounts and KYC. No separate account is required.
Corporate actions such as interest payments and redemptions can be automated through smart contracts under applicable rules.
Tokenised bond issuances by REC Limited, Larsen & Toubro Limited and IIFL have already raised a combined Rs 1,025 crore on the distributed ledger platform.
The official noted that several Western markets still operate on T+2 settlement for conventional securities, with Europe preparing to move to T+1. India, he said, has consistently led in introducing market infrastructure innovations in a regulated manner and remains in a leading position with this development.
Demat 2.0 retains the legal structure, investor rights and regulatory safeguards of the existing demat system while adding atomic settlement and tokenisation capabilities.

India launches Demat 2.0 pilot for tokenized corporate bonds

SEBI and the RBI have launched Demat 2.0, a regulatory-sandbox pilot testing Indian corporate bonds as native digital tokens on a private, permissioned ledger.

The bonds retain their existing ISINs, coupons, maturities and investor rights, while ownership is recorded by statutory depositories NSDL and CDSL. Settlement uses the RBI’s wholesale digital rupee, enabling atomic delivery-versus-payment.

Three issues totaling ₹10.25 billion (approximately $110 million) have already been completed by REC, L&T and IIFL Finance. The pilot currently focuses on institutional issuance, with secondary trading and retail access planned for later stages.

The project is not a new asset class or public crypto product. It tests whether tokenized bonds can improve settlement, automate coupon payments and reduce reconciliation within India’s existing regulated market infrastructure.

Demat 2.0' क्या है और यह कैसे अलग है?

Demat 1.0 (1996): इसने कागजी शेयरों (Paper Shares) को डिजिटल डेटाबेस में बदला था।

Demat 2.0 (2026): यह Blockchain या Distributed Ledger Technology  पर आधारित है,इसके तहत कॉरपोरेट बॉन्ड्स  को डिजिटल टोकन के रूप में जारी किया जा रहा है।

CBDC (Wholesale e₹) से इसका सीधा कनेक्शन
Demat 2.0 का प्लेटफॉर्म RBI के थोक CBDC नेटवर्क से जुड़ा हुआ है।
एटॉमिक सेटलमेंट : इसका मतलब है कि जैसे ही निवेशक को डिजिटल बॉन्ड टोकन ट्रांसफर होगा, वैसे ही उसी पल पैसे का भुगतान CBDC वॉलेट के जरिए हो जाएगा. पहले सेकेंडरी मार्केट में फंड और सिक्योरिटी ट्रांसफर होने में 2 से 3 दिन का समय लगता था, जो अब रियल-टाइम हो जाएगा।

स्मार्ट कॉन्ट्रैक्ट्स' का जादू (ऑटोमैटिक ब्याज)

CBDC और DLT के इस मिलन से सबसे बड़ा फायदा यह होगा कि बॉन्ड पर मिलने वाला ब्याज (Coupon) और मैच्योरिटी का पैसा किसी इंसान या बैंक मैनेजर द्वारा ट्रांसफर नहीं किया जाएगा।

इसमें Smart Contracts (कोडिंग निर्देश) लिखे गए हैं, जैसे ही भुगतान की तारीख आएगी, सिस्टम अपने आप निवेशक के CBDC वॉलेट में पैसा क्रेडिट कर देगा ।
इस पायलट प्रोजेक्ट की शुरुआत REC Limited (₹500 करोड़), L&T (₹500 करोड़), और IIFL (₹25 करोड़) द्वारा टोकनाइज्ड बॉन्ड जारी करके सफलतापूर्वक कर दी गई है, भारत दुनिया का पहला ऐसा देश बन गया है जिसने अपनी मौजूदा कानूनी मार्केट व्यवस्था के भीतर ही टोकनाइज्ड बॉन्ड्स और देश की आधिकारिक डिजिटल करेंसी (CBDC) के सेटलमेंट को एक साथ जोड़ दिया है।

Demat 2.0' के लॉन्च होने के बाद आम रिटेल निवेशकों  के लिए यह व्यवस्था कैसे काम करेगी और भविष्य का रोडमैप क्या है?
पायलट प्रोजेक्ट के सफल परीक्षण के बाद, इसे आम रिटेल निवेशकों के लिए खोल दिया जाएगा. जब यह आपके और हमारे लिए लाइव होगा, तब इसमें भाग लेने की प्रक्रिया बेहद आसान होगी।
आपको कोई नया डीमैट अकाउंट खोलने या नए सिरे से KYC कराने की जरूरत नहीं होगी,आप अपने मौजूदा डीमैट अकाउंट से ही इन डिजिटल टोकनाइज्ड बॉन्ड्स को खरीद सकेंगे

आपको अपने डिपॉजिटरी (NSDL या CDSL) के जरिए 'Demat 2.0' सर्विस को एक्टिवेट करना होगा और अपने बैंक खाते के साथ एक Wholesale CBDC (ई-रुपया) वॉलेट लिंक करना होगा।
आम निवेशकों को इससे क्या 'बड़ा फायदा' मिलेगा?

फ्रैक्शनलाइजेशन (Fractionalisation - छोटे टुकड़ों में निवेश):अभी तक कॉरपोरेट बॉन्ड मार्केट मुख्य रूप से बड़े अमीर लोगों या संस्थाओं का खेल रहा है, क्योंकि एक-एक बॉन्ड की कीमत लाखों रुपये (जैसे ₹10 लाख न्यूनतम) होती है,Demat 2.0 और टोकनाइजेशन की मदद से इन बड़े बॉन्ड्स को ₹100 जैसे छोटे डिजिटल टोकन्स में तोड़ा जा सकेगा. यानी एक आम मध्यमवर्गीय व्यक्ति भी ₹100 या ₹500 से भारत की बड़ी कंपनियों के सुरक्षित बॉन्ड्स में निवेश कर सकेगा।

इंस्टेंट डिलीवरी और नो सेटलमेंट रिस्क:आज जब आप कोई बॉन्ड या शेयर खरीदते हैं, तो पैसे कटने और आपके अकाउंट में सिक्योरिटी आने के बीच समय का अंतर होता है. Demat 2.0 के Atomic Settlement की वजह से जैसे ही आप अपने CBDC वॉलेट से पेमेंट करेंगे, उसी माइक्रो-सेकंड में बॉन्ड आपके डीमैट खाते में आ जाएगा

ब्याज का ऑटोमैटिक क्रेडिट:चूंकि यह पूरा सिस्टम Smart Contracts (कोडिंग) पर चलेगा, इसलिए कंपनी कब ब्याज (Coupon) देगी, इसकी चिंता आपको नहीं करनी है,तय तारीख आते ही ब्लॉकचेन सिस्टम अपने आप आपके CBDC वॉलेट में ब्याज का पैसा ट्रांसफर कर देगा

भविष्य में इस व्यवस्था का दायरा केवल बॉन्ड्स तक सीमित नहीं रहेगा. तीसरे चरण में SEBI और RBI की योजना इसके तहत इक्विटी शेयर्स , म्यूचुअल फंड्स  और गोल्ड (Digital Gold Tokenisation) को भी शामिल करने की है।

🎙️U.S. consumer inflation accelerated in August. Headline CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month and 3.4% year-on-year, while core CPI increased 0.3% MoM, above the 0.2% consensus, and stood at 2.4% YoY. Combined with yesterday's stronger PPI report, the data pushed market pricing for a 25 bp Federal Reserve hike next week to roughly 85%, from around 70% before CPI.

The bond market initially reinforced that message. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached approximately 4.99%, close to the psychologically important 5% level, before easing toward 4.92%. Bitcoin, meanwhile, continued trading around the $77,000 area, while oil retreated from an intraday Brent peak near $110 but remained above $100.

Market significance: The macro sequence is becoming increasingly difficult for risk assets to ignore. Stronger employment, higher producer inflation and now firmer consumer inflation are collectively giving the Fed considerably more room to tighten. Yet Bitcoin has not experienced a disorderly reaction. That does not make the current structure bullish, but it does mean the market is so far absorbing a substantial repricing of interest-rate expectations without a major leverage event. The next question is whether that stability survives if Treasury yields remain near 5%.

🎙️Global investors are simultaneously becoming more defensive. Equity funds recorded approximately $15.52B of net outflows in the week ending September 9, their largest weekly withdrawal since March. U.S. equity funds alone experienced approximately $32.27B of redemptions. At the same time, around $10.72B moved into money-market funds, while short-duration bond funds attracted approximately $6.65B.

Market significance: Crypto weakness is occurring inside a much broader reduction in risk appetite. Capital is not merely moving from Bitcoin into another part of crypto. Investors across conventional markets are shortening duration and moving toward instruments that offer liquidity and yield with less price risk. With risk-free yields approaching levels that can compete directly for capital, speculative assets face a progressively higher hurdle for attracting incremental money.

🎙️India has formally launched Demat 2.0, a joint RBI and SEBI pilot combining tokenized corporate securities, central-bank digital currency settlement and smart contracts. The first phase includes three corporate bond issuances involving Larsen & Toubro, REC and IIFL, with regulated institutions including CDSL, NSDL, BSE, NSE, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and NPCI participating in the broader architecture. The system is designed to enable faster settlement while automating parts of asset servicing such as interest payments and redemptions.

Market significance: This is considerably more important than simply issuing another tokenized bond. India is testing an architecture where the asset is tokenized, settlement occurs using central-bank money and the regulated financial system remains integrated throughout the process. If successfully extended into secondary trading and eventually other asset classes, tokenization begins affecting the actual plumbing of capital markets rather than remaining a parallel blockchain experiment.

🎙️Kalshi is seeking regulatory approval to introduce approximately 60 single-stock and ETF perpetual futures products in the United States, potentially including companies such as Apple, Nvidia and Tesla. Unlike conventional futures contracts, perpetuals have no fixed expiry and have historically been associated primarily with crypto markets. Kalshi has already introduced regulated perpetual products linked to crypto and precious metals.

Market significance: This represents an interesting reversal in the direction of financial innovation. Much of the tokenization discussion focuses on traditional assets moving onto crypto infrastructure. Perpetual futures show the opposite process taking place. A product structure developed and popularized within crypto markets is now being considered for conventional equities under U.S. regulation. Crypto is therefore influencing traditional market design, not merely receiving traditional assets.

🎙️The European Securities and Markets Authority has also warned that increasing connections between crypto and conventional finance create greater potential for interconnectedness and financial spillovers. ESMA highlighted growing tokenized-equity adoption, recent DeFi exploits and prediction markets while warning more broadly that deteriorating macroeconomic conditions and elevated valuations leave financial markets vulnerable to abrupt corrections.

Market significance: The regulatory concern itself is revealing. Historically, regulators were primarily concerned with losses occurring inside crypto markets. The discussion is increasingly shifting toward whether crypto has become connected enough to banks, securities markets, asset managers and payment infrastructure that instability could eventually move between the two systems. That concern only becomes relevant once integration reaches meaningful scale.

My Own Viewpoint:
Two processes are happening simultaneously, and separating them is becoming increasingly important.

Financial infrastructure is becoming more crypto-like while the macro environment is becoming less friendly to risk.

India is combining tokenized securities with central-bank money. Kalshi wants to bring perpetual futures into conventional equities. Regulators are beginning to discuss crypto in the context of financial-system interconnectedness.

These are structural developments. They do not disappear because Bitcoin falls a few percentage points.

But the other side of the market cannot be ignored.

Inflation remains persistent. The probability of another Federal Reserve hike has increased sharply. Treasury yields are challenging 5%. Oil remains above $100. Global investors are withdrawing money from equities and moving capital into money-market and shorter-duration instruments.

That means the opportunity cost of holding risk assets is rising at exactly the same time that crypto's underlying financial infrastructure is becoming more institutional.

This creates a distinction I think matters considerably:
Adoption and liquidity are not the same thing.

The infrastructure can continue improving while financial conditions suppress asset prices. Equally, weak prices do not automatically mean that the underlying adoption cycle has reversed.

For now, crypto's structural integration continues to advance, while the price of capital continues to move against it.

The market will eventually have to reconcile those two forces.

Can a company reporting a net loss of ₹12 crore actually be generating ₹116 crore of quarterly cash profit?

Horizon Industrial Parks reported its first post-listing numbers for Q1 FY27. Revenue reached ₹200 crore, up 23% YoY, while EBITDA expanded 36% to ₹161 crore with an 80% operating margin. Yet the bottom line printed a ₹12 crore loss.

The tension on the call was immediate: how quickly does the P&L reflect the company's transformed balance sheet?

Management explained that the reported loss is purely an accounting artifact of ₹75 crore non-cash depreciation and legacy interest costs. Following its ₹4,250 crore IPO capital raise, the company paid down ₹3,900 crore of debt, cutting pro forma net debt to ₹2,500 crore (12.5% of enterprise value). Factoring in those interest savings, pro forma quarterly cash profit stands at ₹116 crore, with accounting profit guided to turn positive by Q2/Q3 FY27.

Operationally, the engine is running fast. Horizon leased 1.9M sq ft in Q1—three-quarters to industrial manufacturing tenants at a 15-20% rental premium—taking its contracted revenue run-rate to ₹970 crore across 29.5M sq ft operational area. Full-year leasing is guided at 6.5M sq ft (~30% YoY growth), backed by a fully paid 2,300-acre land bank that can double capacity to 61M sq ft over 4-5 years.

Do the math on their expansion: Horizon plans ₹1,500-2,000 crore capex over 3 years. With internal accruals generating ~₹464 crore in annualized cash PAT against an equity funding ask of ~₹500-660 crore (1/3rd of capex), the buildout is comfortably self-funding.

However, a key friction point emerged in Q&A: 13 in-city warehouse tenders partnering with Central Warehousing Corporation are currently challenged in the Delhi High Court. Management cited sub-judice rules and declined to elaborate, even as they target a 13-14% yield on cost from that format.

Delivery of the maiden Pune in-city facility in Q4 FY27, resolution of the tender litigation, and accounting PAT turning black next quarter are the milestones to track.

เมื่อวันพฤหัสบดีที่ผ่านมา คณะกรรมการกำกับหลักทรัพย์และตลาดหลักทรัพย์ของอินเดีย หรือ SEBI ระบุว่าระบบ Demat 2.0 นี้ ช่วยให้สามารถออกและถือครองพันธบัตรองค์กรในรูปแบบโทเคนดิจิทัลบนบัญชีแยกประเภทแบบกระจายศูนย์ (Distributed Ledger) ซึ่งดูแลโดยหน่วยงานรับฝากหลักทรัพย์ของประเทศ โดยระบบนี้เชื่อมต่อกับสกุลเงินดิจิทัลของธนาคารกลาง (CBDC) ประเภทขายส่งของธนาคารกลางอินเดีย (RBI) ผ่านอินเทอร์เฟซตลาดแบบรวมศูนย์
